definitions.explanation: tending to obey or yield to others without resistance, often implying excessive passivity

examples.japanese: {服従的|ふくじゅうてき}な{態度|たいど}をとった。
あまりに{服従的|ふくじゅうてき}な{姿勢|しせい}は{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: Being too compliant is a problem.

examples.japanese: {権力|けんりょく}に{対|たい}して{服従的|ふくじゅうてき}であることが{美徳|びとく}とされた{時代|じだい}もあった。
examples.english: There was a time when being submissive to authority was considered a virtue.

notes:
Composed of {服従|ふくじゅう} (obedience/submission) and {的|てき} (adjectival suffix). Describes someone who follows orders or yields to authority without resistance. Can be used neutrally (describing obedient behavior) or negatively (criticizing excessive passivity). The base noun {服従|ふくじゅう} carries a stronger connotation of subordination.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {服従的|ふくじゅうてき}な{態度|たいど}: submissive attitude
- {服従的|ふくじゅうてき}な{姿勢|しせい}: compliant posture/stance
- {服従的|ふくじゅうてき}な{性格|せいかく}: submissive personality
- {服従的|ふくじゅうてき}になる: to become submissive

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {従順|じゅうじゅん}: obedient, docile — emphasizes willingness to follow, often positive
- {消極的|しょうきょくてき}: passive — broader, meaning lacking initiative in general
- {卑屈|ひくつ}: servile, self-deprecating — negative, implies groveling
